items.project_definition: The set of rejected architectural paths, such as direct dialect usage in business logic or heavyweight object-relational mapping, used to justify the final selection.
The four foundational persistent storage mutation primitives validated via in-memory storage.
A high-level wrapper for low-level concurrency failures originating from the storage engine.
The definitive architectural choice made to resolve a design trade-off.
A business-level exception thrown when a requested record is missing from the persistence layer.
Full-stack verification executing command-line interfaces against temporary file-based storage.
An abstraction layer for mapping objects to tables, explicitly rejected to maintain minimal overhead.
The raw engine-specific failure signal that must be caught and transformed by the data access layer.
The logical justification supporting a specific design choice based on modularity or performance.
A class-based abstraction managing a database connection to isolate the query dialect from the core logic.
Isolated unit validations using non-persistent memory for rapid execution.
The raw structured query language used for fine-grained transaction control.
The middle layer responsible for orchestration, business validation, and translating storage errors into domain exceptions.
Logic validations using simulated data access layers to eliminate disk dependencies.
A development cycle focusing on creating tests before functional implementation to ensure a tight feedback loop.
The presentation layer, specifically the command-line interface, which transforms exceptions into human-readable messages.
A business-layer failure indicating that the input data violates system constraints.
The engineering principle of avoiding the implementation of features until they are strictly necessary to maintain simplicity.
